sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: We started when a local guild went on video for one winter and half of it never went back.

sections.heading: No meeting hall required
sections.html:
Our members live on farms, in dorms, and on two continents. What holds the guild together is a shared calendar, a mailing list that stays on topic, and a rule that show and tell belongs to everyone: photos count as much as live video.

We keep one foot on the ground, too. Chapters of two or three meet in person where they can, and the annual retreat is the weekend the whole guild finally shares a room.

items.title: Winter
items.body: The retreat weekend and the design-wall challenge, announced in January.

items.title: Spring
items.body: Guest teachers over video, one per month, recorded for the library.

items.title: Summer
items.body: Sew-along season: one quilt, ten weeks, a thread for every step.

items.title: Fall
items.body: The mail-swap reveal meeting and elections that take eleven minutes.

items.quote: I have not missed a meeting since I joined, and I live four hours from the nearest guild hall.
items.author: Rosa, member since 2021

items.quote: My mail-swap partner sent orchid fabric from Hawaii. My block went to Nova Scotia.

sections.title: Programs and workshops
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Teachers join by video, supply lists post a month ahead, and kits ship where shipping beats driving.

sections.heading: How a workshop runs
sections.html: Register on the event page and the supply list arrives by email. Kit orders ship the week before class. Workshops are recorded and stay in the member library, so a time zone is never a disqualification.

sections.title: Show and tell
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: The last half hour of every meeting. Photos welcome, wobbly first blocks encouraged.

sections.heading: How it works on a screen
sections.html: Hold the quilt close to the camera, then step back so we can see the whole top. Say who pieced it, who quilted it, and what you learned. Send photos ahead to the moderator if your connection is slow, and they will run the slide while you talk.

sections.title: Bees that never need a ride
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Small groups on video, one evening bee per time zone, and swaps that keep the mailbox interesting.

items.title: Atlantic bee
items.body: Tuesdays at 7 Eastern. Hand piecing and shop talk, cameras down by eight.

items.title: Central bee
items.body: Wednesdays at 7. Machine piecing with a monthly technique warm-up.

items.title: Pacific bee
items.body: Thursdays at 7. Long, chatty, and the origin of the guild's mending nights.

items.title: The swap table
items.body: Quarterly mail swaps matched by the swap chair. Postcard quilts in October.

sections.heading: New to bees
sections.html: Every bee keeps two open seats for new members, and the swap chair matches first-timers with a partner who has been warned that you are new. That is the whole initiation.

sections.title: Membership in {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Thirty dollars a year, no hall to drive to, and a guild that meets you where your machine is plugged in.

sections.heading: What dues cover
sections.html: Monthly meetings and their recordings, every bee, the workshop library, swap matching, and the retreat registration discount. Open the membership form and pick a level; the welcome email includes the next meeting link and the current sew-along thread.

items.q: Do I have to be on camera?
items.a: No. Plenty of members sew along with cameras off and send photos for show and tell instead.

items.q: I am not in the United States. Can I join?
items.a: Yes. We have members in Canada, the UK, and Australia. Workshops post in three time zones on the calendar.
Any time, from the members portal. Dues are not prorated, but the recording library stays open through the year you paid for.

sections.title: Write to {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Program pitches, swap questions, and press requests all land in the same inbox, answered between stitches.

sections.heading: For the mail swaps
sections.html: Swap parcels go to the guild post office box listed in the newsletter. Put your forum name on the return label so your partner can thank the right quilter.
